subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw adopt for side-effecting exec secret providers under service supervisors?
rationale: The current fail-fast startup contract is documented and security-sensitive, while retry/backoff/circuit-breaker behavior can reduce provider-rate amplification but also changes credential-provider execution timing and may require new config or operator guidance.

options.title: Generic bounded startup protection
options.body: Add owner-approved generic retry/backoff or restart-storm mitigation for exec SecretRef activation without hardcoding 1Password, plus tests and docs for fresh startup and supervisor recovery.

options.title: Docs and doctor guidance first
options.body: Keep runtime fail-fast behavior and document supervisor restart-throttle guidance plus 1Password batching/caching resolver advice.

options.title: Provider/plugin integration path
options.body: Defer core retry policy and route external vault batching/caching to a plugin or ClawHub resolver while keeping this issue as the missing-core-policy tracker.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup protection
recommendation.body: Add owner-approved generic retry/backoff or restart-storm mitigation for exec SecretRef activation without hardcoding 1Password, plus tests and docs for fresh startup and supervisor recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history signal for external SecretRef provider behavior and eager activation.
